topics: Basics of Randomization - Introduction to randomized algorithms, Probabilistic analysis and expectations, Benefits and applications of randomization.
Probability Review - Basic probability theory, Random variables and distributions, Linearity of expectation.
Basic Randomized Algorithms - Randomized quicksort, Randomized selection, Randomized data structures.
Randomized Graph Algorithms - Randomized algorithms for graph problems, Minimum cut problems, Randomized algorithms for network flows.
Hashing and Randomized Data Structures - Universal and perfect hashing, Skip lists, Bloom filters.
Markov Chains and Random Walks - Introduction to Markov chains, Random walks on graphs, Applications in randomized algorithms.
The Probabilistic Method - Basics of the probabilistic method, Linearity of expectation, First and second-moment methods.
Chernoff Bounds and Concentration Inequalities - Markov's inequality, Chebyshev's inequality, Chernoff bounds, Applications of concentration inequalities.
Randomized Rounding and Martingales - Randomized rounding techniques, Applications in approximation algorithms, Introduction to martingales, Azuma's inequality.
Randomized Complexity Classes - RP, ZPP, and BPP, Relationships between complexity classes, Amplification and derandomization techniques

courseOutcomes.description: Demonstrate a strong understanding of the basics of randomized algorithms, including probabilistic analysis, expectations, and the benefits of randomization
Illustrate basic randomized algorithms, such as randomized quicksort, selection, and data structures, and evaluate their performance against deterministic alternatives.
Apply advanced randomized techniques, including randomized graph algorithms, hashing, and Markov chains, to address complex graph and data structure problems.

Show expertise in probabilistic methods, including Chernoff bounds, concentration inequalities, and randomized rounding, and use these methods to solve approximation and analysis problems in algorithms
Understand and apply concepts related to randomized complexity classes, such as RP, ZPP, and BPP, and explore amplification and derandomization techniques
